title: whats-new-in-rezure-3-1
content: <p>Rezure has changed a lot since our docs last caught up. The app you install today runs PostgreSQL and SQL Server next to MariaDB, catches your outgoing email, switches Node.js versions per project, and keeps PHP running under load. This post walks through everything that has landed in the 3.x line, up to <strong>Rezure 3.1.1</strong>.</p><p>Already on Rezure 3? Open the <strong>Changelog</strong> page and press <strong>Update</strong>. New here? Grab the installer from the <a href="/download">download page</a>.</p><h2>More databases: PostgreSQL and SQL Server</h2><h3>PostgreSQL, next to MariaDB</h3><p>PostgreSQL <strong>18, 17 and 16</strong> can be installed from inside Rezure. They are portable builds, so there is no installer to click through and nothing written into Windows. Removing PostgreSQL means deleting a folder.</p><ul><li>It runs as its own service on port <code>5432</code>, at the same time as MariaDB. You no longer have to pick one.</li><li>Each major version gets its own data directory, because PostgreSQL can only open data created by the same major.</li><li>A <code>root</code> role is created for you, so a Laravel project with <code>DB_CONNECTION=pgsql</code> connects without changing the username or setting a password. Like MariaDB in Rezure, it only listens on <code>127.0.0.1</code>.</li><li>PostgreSQL databases show up on the <strong>Databases</strong> page.</li></ul><blockquote><p>PostgreSQL refuses to start from an elevated process. If you launched Rezure with "Run as administrator", start it normally instead. Rezure tells you this up front rather than failing silently.</p></blockquote><h3>SQL Server for PHP projects</h3><p>If your PHP project talks to SQL Server, which is common in corporate, government, banking and ERP work, you used to spend an afternoon hunting for the right driver DLLs. Rezure now installs the whole chain:</p><ol><li><strong>The PHP drivers</strong> (<code>sqlsrv</code> and <code>pdo_sqlsrv</code>), matched to each PHP version. No admin rights needed.</li><li><strong>Microsoft ODBC Driver 18</strong>, which the PHP drivers need. Rezure downloads Microsoft's official installer and runs it after you accept the license yourself. Windows asks for admin rights once.</li><li><strong>SQL Server LocalDB</strong>, optional, if you want a SQL Server on your own machine. It runs as a normal user process, so starting and stopping it does not trigger a UAC prompt every time.</li></ol><p>You can also add a SQL Server connection, local or remote, on the <strong>Databases</strong> page. One honest caveat: the ODBC Driver and LocalDB are Microsoft installers, so they live in Windows' Apps list and stay installed if you uninstall Rezure.</p><h2>Catch every email with Mailpit</h2><p>Testing password resets and notifications should not mean sending real emails. Rezure can now run <strong>Mailpit</strong>, a local mail catcher. Install it from the Services page with one click, start it, and point your project at it:</p><ul><li><code>MAIL_MAILER=smtp</code></li><li><code>MAIL_HOST=127.0.0.1</code></li><li><code>MAIL_PORT=1025</code></li></ul><p>Every email your app sends lands in an inbox at <code>http://127.0.0.1:8025</code> (the <strong>Open</strong> button on the Mailpit card takes you there). Caught emails survive a restart, and Mailpit accepts any username and password, so a <code>.env</code> that still holds your real provider's credentials works as long as the host and port point at Mailpit.</p><p>The project <strong>Requirements check</strong> reads your mail settings too. It spots the two classic mistakes: Laravel's default <code>MAIL_PORT=2525</code>, and <code>MAIL_HOST=mailpit</code> copied from a Docker Sail setup, which does not resolve outside Docker.</p><h2>Node.js versions, globally or per project</h2><p>Node.js now has its own row on the <strong>Switch</strong> page. Rezure offers the newest release of every LTS line plus the newest Current release, and shows the npm version that comes with each one.</p><p>Pick a global version for everyday use, then pin a different one on any project from its project card. When you open a terminal from that project card, <code>node</code>, <code>npm</code> and <code>npx</code> are the pinned version. Nothing else on your system changes.</p><h2>One "Install version" button for every runtime</h2><p>The <strong>Install version</strong> button on the Switch page used to be PHP-only. It now covers PHP, Nginx, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, Mailpit, SQL Server LocalDB, Composer and Node.js. Choose the runtime, then the version.</p><p>Version lists come from each project's own release feed where one exists (php.net, MariaDB's download API, getcomposer.org, nodejs.org), and every portable runtime is checked against a SHA-256 checksum before it is unpacked. The dropdown on each runtime row is now for switching only: it lists what you have installed, nothing else.</p><h2>PHP Extensions, without editing php.ini</h2><p>A new <strong>PHP Extensions</strong> page sits right under Switch in the sidebar. Choose a PHP version and turn extensions on or off with a switch: <code>bcmath</code>, <code>gmp</code>, <code>sodium</code>, <code>exif</code>, <code>sockets</code>, <code>ldap</code>, <code>opcache</code> and about thirty more, grouped by category and searchable.</p><ul><li>Your choices are saved per PHP version, so turning on <code>gmp</code> for 8.3 does not touch 7.4.</li><li>Extensions missing from a particular PHP build are marked <strong>not in this build</strong> instead of failing quietly.</li><li><code>opcache</code> is off by default, since a stale cache can hide the code change you just made.</li><li>If PHP is running when you flip a switch, Rezure reminds you to restart it.</li></ul><p>Need <code>redis</code>? It is not shipped with PHP, so the Requirements check offers an <strong>Install</strong> button that fetches a verified build for your PHP version.</p><h2>PHP that stays up</h2><p>Some users saw occasional <strong>502 Bad Gateway</strong> errors under real workloads. We tracked down every cause and fixed it:</p><ul><li><strong>PHP no longer quits after 500 requests.</strong> That was a built-in default of <code>php-cgi</code>, and the cause of most of the 502s.</li><li><strong>A slow request no longer blocks the rest.</strong> On Windows, one <code>php-cgi</code> process handles one request at a time, so each PHP version now runs a small pool of workers.</li><li><strong>PHP restarts itself if it crashes</strong>, waiting a little longer after each crash. If it crashes five times in five minutes, Rezure stops retrying so you can look at the log.</li><li><strong>Bigger uploads and longer requests.</strong> Uploads up to 64 MB and scripts up to 300 seconds work out of the box, instead of hitting "413 Request Entity Too Large" at 1 MB.</li><li><strong>HTTPS calls from PHP just work.</strong> Rezure ships an up-to-date CA certificate bundle and sets it in <code>php.ini</code> for you, and the Requirements check now tests an HTTPS call from your project's PHP.</li></ul><h2>Show only the services you use</h2><p>With more services on offer, the Services page could get crowded. The new <strong>Manage services</strong> button lets you remove the cards you never use, so a MySQL user can hide SQL Server, and the reverse. Removing a card only hides it: binaries, data and connections stay where they are, and you can add the card back at any time. <strong>Start all</strong> and <strong>Stop all</strong> follow your list.</p><h2>Make it yours: themes and stickers</h2><p>The new <strong>Appearance</strong> page offers fourteen themes in three groups, Default, Girls and Mens, from the original coral Rezure to glass themes, Lavender Dream, Matcha, Carbon, Forest and a green-on-black Terminal. You can also tune brightness, color intensity, glass opacity and UI size, or reduce motion. Light and dark mode live on the button in the title bar.</p><p>And if you want a pink bow on your sidebar, you can have one. <strong>Decorations</strong> lets you place stickers anywhere in the window. Two dozen come built in, and <strong>Browse</strong> downloads more from our catalog.</p><h2>Your AI coding agent now knows about Rezure</h2><p>AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Cursor know Laragon from their training data, but not Rezure. On a machine with both, an agent that runs <code>where php</code> would often go looking for Laragon.</p><p>Rezure now keeps an <code>AGENTS.md</code> (plus a <code>CLAUDE.md</code> that points to it) in its home folder. It describes your machine as it is right now: the active PHP version, the database setup, and every project with its URL, folder and the PHP version that actually serves it. A longer guide explains ports, folders, <code>php.ini</code> layers and the house rules, for example "don't start or kill Rezure's processes yourself". Rezure updates these files when things change, and projects inside <code>www</code> pick them up automatically.</p><h2>Updates from inside the app</h2><p>When a new version is out, a red dot appears on <strong>Changelog</strong> in the sidebar. Open it and press <strong>Update</strong>: Rezure downloads the installer, shows the progress, and hands over to it.</p><p>Every update is signed, and Rezure checks the signature against a key built into the app before running anything. An installer that was changed by even a single bit is rejected.</p><h2>Fixed in 3.1.1: freeing a busy port</h2><p>When a port Rezure needs is taken, the service card offers to stop whatever holds it. With Nginx or MySQL 8 that did not always work: the process you stopped was a child, and its parent immediately started a new one on the same port. Rezure now stops the parent, so the port stays free.</p><h2>What's next</h2><p>Next on the list are Xdebug as a first-class extension, supervised queue workers for your projects, a project health dashboard, and Redis as a service. Over the coming weeks we will also cover each feature above in its own article, with step-by-step setup.</p><p>Found a bug, or missing something you use every day? Send it through the <strong>Feedback</strong> page in the app. We read every report.</p>
